questions.question: Define hazard, disaster and vulnerability, and use the 2010 Haiti and Chile earthquakes to explain why vulnerability matters.
questions.expected_answer: Hazard: a natural event that could cause harm. Disaster: when a hazard causes serious loss of life and damage beyond a community's ability to cope. Vulnerability: how easily people can be harmed. Haiti's magnitude 7 earthquake killed well over 100 000 people because of poorly built buildings, poverty, crowding and weak services; Chile's much stronger magnitude 8.8 earthquake killed about 500 because of strict building codes, preparation and resources.

questions.question: Describe four ways of reducing the impact of earthquakes before they happen.
questions.expected_answer: Earthquake-resistant buildings (steel reinforcement, cross-bracing, base isolators, dampers); enforced building codes; retrofitting schools, hospitals and bridges; land-use planning avoiding faults, steep slopes and soft soils; early warning and tsunami warning systems; education and drills (drop, cover, hold on); household emergency kits and plans; gas shut-off valves.

questions.question: Explain what should happen in the response and recovery stages after an earthquake.
questions.expected_answer: Response: rapid search and rescue in the first 72 hours, medical care and field hospitals, emergency shelter, clean water, food and sanitation to prevent disease, firefighting, securing dangerous buildings, restoring communications, international aid. Recovery: rebuilding homes, infrastructure and the economy over years, building back better to higher standards, and supporting mental health.
